data.q: Is my data safe? Can other shops see it?
data.a: No. Every shop's data is separate and backed up every night. Only your staff, with the roles you give them, can see your shop.

phone.a: No. It runs on any Android phone (app or browser) and on iPhone / laptop in the browser. A thermal printer is optional.

offline.a: Keep selling. Sales, stock and payments wait on the phone and are sent when the connection returns.

staff.q: Can my salesman see the buying price?
staff.a: Only if you want. Owner, manager, salesman and technician each see what you allow.

cancel.a: Yes. Pay month by month; your data stays yours and can be downloaded as Excel at any time.

scanner.a: Any USB or Bluetooth scanner that types like a keyboard — most do, and they cost about three to eight thousand rupees. Plug it in and scan, no setup. Without one, the phone camera reads IMEIs and barcodes too.

android.a: Yes. Download it from this page (Download the app) and install it on any Android phone. The same account also opens in any browser on a laptop or iPhone.

verify.q: How does it check a used phone?
verify.a: When you buy a used phone you scan the seller's CNIC, note the PTA status and the IMEI; tablets and watches also need the iCloud / Google lock check. Until the check is done the phone cannot be sold; skipping needs a reason that the owner sees.

consent.a: The person selling you a used phone signs a declaration on the screen that the phone is his and not stolen. It is saved with his CNIC, the IMEI and the date, and can be printed any time.

yearly.a: Yes. Pay for a year at once and get 12 months for the price of 10 — two months free. Monthly payment is also there.

fbr.a: Yes. Every bill already reads like a tax invoice. For sales-tax registered shops the app sends each bill to FBR's Digital Invoicing system and prints the FBR number and QR. It is off by default; you need your NTN, STRN and the IRIS token, and we switch it on with you after a sandbox test.

branches.q: I have two shops. Can I see both?
branches.a: Yes. One login can open all your shops; each keeps its own stock, khata and reports, and you can send stock from one to the other with a branch transfer.

landing.newTitle: What came in the last round
landing.newSub: Built from what shopkeepers asked for — the newest first, all included, in Urdu and English.

fbr.d: Every bill can go to FBR by itself and print the FBR number with its QR code. Off until your NTN and IRIS token are in; if the internet is down the bill waits and goes later.

taxbill.d: Amount in words (lakh / crore), cashier and time, total excl. tax, tax by rate and total tax — the way an FBR tax invoice reads. Phones under the Ninth Schedule can be left untaxed.

cashchange.d: Type what the customer handed over; the screen shows the change and the bill prints both.

books.d: What the shop owns, owes and is worth on any date, and every account side by side — straight from the same entries as every other report.

transfers.d: Send phones and items from one shop to another. Each phone keeps its history in both shops; items move at cost, so neither branch shows a fake profit.

repairlink.d: The customer gets a link on WhatsApp and sees their phone's repair status — received, at the lab, ready — without calling the shop.

accounts.d: Stock never goes into minus by a typed item, returns leave stock at stock value, and a loss always shows with its minus sign.

audit.d: Profit, cash & bank, udhaar, stock and staff for any dates — opening, closing and as-of balances, every figure tappable to its bills, checks that catch mistakes, a complete report as PDF or Excel.

bulk.d: Bring 300 old phones, your khata, accessories, sales and expenses in one sheet. Sample rows to copy, a check before anything is saved, and the same sheet back out.

history.d: What it cost, what it sold for, every payment and price change on one screen; every person's phones and payments on theirs — downloadable and shareable in every format.

prices.d: The asking price is set at purchase; a change at the sale is recorded with the reason, and your rules decide who may sell under it — with the owner's PIN if you want.

ai.d: Ask in Urdu or English: "how much did Ahmed owe last month?" — answered from your shop's data. A photo of the CNIC or the box label fills the form.

home.d: Fast actions first, then today's sales, profit, cash, udhaar and stock with charts — what a shopkeeper looks at ten times a day.

installments.d: Sell on monthly installments with the advance, the plan and reminders for each due date.

hazri.d: In and out with the phone, late marks, the month's hazri sheet per employee.

otp.d: A code on WhatsApp resets the password; nobody has to call.

windows.d: A shop without internet can run everything on one Windows PC with a setup file and nightly backups.

barcode.t: Barcode on every unit, any scanner
barcode.d: Each phone and item gets its own barcode the moment you buy it; labels print in your size. Plug in any USB or Bluetooth scanner: scan to sell, scan to find, scan the box's IMEI into a purchase.

items.t: Accessories by the dozen, sold by the piece
items.d: Buy 5 dozen cables at Rs. 1,200 a dozen — stock shows 60 pieces at Rs. 100 each. Brand, quality, fits which phone, wholesale and minimum price; every purchase batch kept with what is still left.

devices.t: Tablets & smart watches, one by one
devices.d: Wi-Fi or SIM, RAM, storage, battery health, case size and the full spec sheet — your model library fills it the next time. The same history, bills and khata as phones.

lock.d: A used tablet or watch is bought only after iCloud / Google / paired-device locks are checked; a device with a lock still on cannot be sold. Every check is on its history with who and when.

count.d: Scan everything on the shelf; the app tells you what is missing and what should not be there.

itemreports.t: Item reports & a ready order list
itemreports.d: Low stock grouped by supplier with what to order, stock value at cost and at sale price, fast and slow items, dead stock, profit by brand — and change prices by % in one go.

reminders.t: Clear plan reminders, data never locked
reminders.d: A calm bar before your plan ends, pay from the app with the bank details shown, and even after the date you can still pay, export and download a full backup.

repairlabs.d: Send a phone to Zain Lab or Ali Lab and record it: who has it, since when, the rate. Back fixed or not, the lab's charge goes on its khata. Every lab's record: phones sent, fixed %, days, what you owe.

sticker.d: Print a sticker for the customer's phone: job no., barcode, customer, model, IMEI, problem, ready date. Pick the fields before printing; scan it to open the job.

lending.d: Money given to or taken from a person with no bill: kept apart from bills, adjusted against a later sale, with a return date and a WhatsApp reminder.

help.t: A "?" with an example on everything
help.d: Every field, card and tab has a small "?" that explains it in Urdu, Roman Urdu or English, with a real shop example. Over 1,100 explanations.

trade.d: Paid at the counter vs on udhaar, paid / part / unpaid bills, per employee and per customer, with print and Excel on every screen.

repairaudit.d: Phones in and out, repair income, parts, lab charges and real repair profit, every lab's fixed %, late jobs and phones late at a lab.

roles.d: A salesman can sell, add stock, take returns and money in / out — but never sees buying prices, profit or the shop's audit.

gst.d: An item with its own GST % is taxed at that rate on a taxed bill; the bill says "Tax (by item)". Phones keep the bill's rate.

appearance.d: Light or dark, four designs of the dashboard (Classic, Tiles, Simple, Bold), your own main colour, bigger text and rounder or sharper corners — each PC and phone keeps its own look.

billqr.d: The customer scans the bill and sees it online: items, total, paid and what is left. No name, phone, cost or khata is ever shown.

editdelete.d: A wrong expense, payment, len-den, return or stock change is corrected or deleted from its own row. Before a delete the app says what will happen to stock, galla and khata, with an example. Nothing is wiped — it stays as Deleted.

editbill.t: Fix a sale or purchase bill
editbill.d: Wrong price, phone or payment on a bill? Open it, change what is wrong and save. The old bill stays as Deleted and the corrected one takes its place — stock, galla and khata follow.

stockeasy.d: Search on top with × to clear, one Filters button with tick boxes (several brands, conditions, PTA at once), every filter shown as a chip with ×, and the totals of what you are looking at.

phonepage.t: A phone's page with its sticker
phonepage.d: Everything about the phone in one card — both IMEIs, RAM, condition, PTA, who it came from, who bought it — each with its button beside it. Tick what goes on the sticker and see it before you print.

locked.d: Buy a locked phone without an IMEI, keep it apart in stock, sell it as it is or use it for parts — its cost goes into the profit report.

repairwho.t: Repairs: own technician or outside lab
repairwho.d: Every repair starts with who will do it. Lab price, return date, paid and owed are tracked; shop-repair and lab reports print on A4 for any period.

a4reports.t: Business and audit reports on A4
a4reports.d: The business overview and the shop audit as full A4 reports for the period you choose — PDF, Excel or print, with your shop's header.

loginsafe.d: Only phones the owner allows can log in, every password / PIN change is on record (never the password itself), and login works with password or PIN.

pricelists.d: One tap makes a price list for staff or customers from your stock; an IMEI is checked on PTA's DIRBS and the answer saved on the phone.

landing.guideSub: Every module in two ways: in plain shop words with an example, and how it works inside for the technical reader. Tap a module to open it.

sell.d: Pick the Galaxy A55, the price fills itself.

bill.d: Confirm; the bill is ready to print or WhatsApp.

audit.d: Sales, profit, cash and udhaar for the month.

stock.d: Every phone with its IMEI, status and price.

khata.d: Who owes you and whom you owe.

hisaab.d: What came in, what went out, what is in the galla.

labs.d: A lab's record and the repairs audit.

help.d: Any word explained with an example.

sale.s: Sell a phone or item in a few taps: cash, online, cheque, from abroad, udhaar or installments.
sale.e: Bilal buys an Infinix Hot 40 for Rs. 34,500, pays Rs. 20,000 on Easypaisa: the bill prints, Rs. 14,500 goes on his khata, the phone leaves stock.
sale.x1: One sale writes the bill, its lines and one balanced ledger entry (sales, tax, cost of goods, cash / bank / party).
sale.x2: Each phone gets an immutable "sold" event; stock and its cost are derived, never typed.
sale.x3: Below the asking price or below cost needs the owner / manager PIN (price rules per shop).

purchase.s: Buy phones and items from a dealer, or a used phone from a customer, paid now or on the dealer's udhaar.
purchase.e: Rehman Traders sends 2 Tecno phones at Rs. 28,500 each, you pay Rs. 40,000: Rs. 17,000 is on his khata, both phones are in stock with a barcode.
purchase.x1: Each line opens a device (IMEI-unique per shop) or an item batch at its landed cost.
purchase.x2: Ledger: stock at cost against cash and the supplier's account; returns to the dealer are reversing entries.
purchase.x3: A used phone from a customer needs the ID check (CNIC) before it can be sold.

stock.s: Every phone with its IMEI, PTA status, condition, price and full history from purchase to sale.
stock.e: Search 4512: the iPhone 13 whose IMEI ends in 4512 opens with when it was bought, from whom, its price changes and who it was sold to.
stock.x1: Status comes from a state machine (in stock, sold, at a shop, in repair, returned…); every change is an event row.
stock.x2: The history screen is built only from those events, so it can never disagree with the books.
stock.x3: Tablets and smart watches are the same device record with a type and a spec sheet.

verify.s: Before selling a used phone, check the seller: CNIC, phone of the seller, IMEI not blocked.
verify.e: Usman sells you a used Redmi: you scan his CNIC, note the PTA status; the phone shows "ID check done" before it can be sold.
verify.x1: A device carries a verification status (pending / done / flagged); a pending one blocks the sale.
verify.x2: Skipping it needs a reason ("I know this person") and is listed in the owner-only security audit.
verify.x3: The CNIC photo is stored privately per shop.

khata.s: One page per person: everything sold to or bought from them on udhaar, every payment, and the balance.
khata.e: Bilal's khata: two phones on udhaar Rs. 46,000, paid Rs. 26,000 → you will get Rs. 20,000; WhatsApp him a reminder in one tap.
khata.x1: Balances are derived from an append-only ledger; nothing is ever edited — a correction is a new reversing entry.
khata.x2: Ageing by the oldest unpaid bill, overdue only after a promise date.
khata.x3: A statement downloads as PDF / Excel for any period.

lending.s: Money you give a person or take from them with no bill, kept apart from bills, with a return date and reminders.
lending.e: You lend Tariq Rs. 25,000, back by the 5th; he returns Rs. 10,000. The card shows Rs. 15,000 open; on the 6th a WhatsApp reminder goes out.
lending.x1: A payment with purpose "lending" in the same khata, posted under its own ledger type so every report keeps it apart.
lending.x2: Open len-den is derived (unallocated lent − borrowed); "adjust against bills" moves no money, only bill status.
lending.x3: Return-date reminders run in the night job, at most every 3 days.

payments.s: Galla, bank, Easypaisa, JazzCash and cheques each have their own balance; every payment lands in the right one.
payments.e: A customer sends Rs. 10,000 on Easypaisa: the Easypaisa balance goes up, not the galla. Move Rs. 1,00,000 from galla to HBL in one tap.
payments.x1: Each account is a ledger account; transfers are their own entries and are never income or expense.
payments.x2: Online / cheque / remittance details (TID, bank, rate) are stored with the payment.
payments.x3: The day close compares the counted galla with the expected one and keeps the difference.

returns.s: A customer returns a phone (full refund or with a cut), you return one to the dealer, or swap old for new.
returns.e: A customer returns a phone of Rs. 10,000; you give back Rs. 9,000 and keep Rs. 1,000: the phone is back in stock, Rs. 1,000 is other income.
returns.x1: A return is a new document reversing the sale's share; the original bill is never changed.
returns.x2: The phone gets a "returned" event and is sellable again.
returns.x3: Exchanges post the difference in one entry.

repairs.s: Take a phone in, fix it or send it to a lab in the market, print its sticker, give it back with the bill.
repairs.e: Ahmed's iPhone 11 screen: you take Rs. 3,000 advance, send it to Zain Lab (Rs. 8,500), it comes back fixed; Ahmed gets a "ready" message.
repairs.x1: A job has a status flow; every lab trip is its own row (sent, back fixed / not fixed, cancelled) with full history.
repairs.x2: The lab's charge goes to its khata; on a customer's phone it is a cost of the repair, on the shop's phone it is added to that phone's cost.
repairs.x3: The sticker's barcode is the job number; the screen lock is never printed.

items.s: Chargers, cables, covers, glass: bought by the dozen or box, sold by the piece, with low-stock alerts.
items.e: Buy 3 dozen cables at Rs. 1,200 a dozen: 36 pieces at Rs. 100 each. Sell 6: the stock shows 30 and the profit is right.
items.x1: Every incoming movement opens a batch; outgoing ones empty the oldest first (FIFO) or use the average cost, per shop.
items.x2: Minimum price, wholesale price for dealers, promo price, and an own GST %.
items.x3: Adjustments need a reason; nothing on an item is ever deleted.

installments.s: Sell on monthly installments with a guarantor; see who is due today and who is late.
installments.e: A phone of Rs. 60,000, Rs. 15,000 now and 6 installments of Rs. 7,500 on the 10th; a reminder goes a day before.
installments.x1: The plan only says how the udhaar is paid back; the money stays in the customer's khata.
installments.x2: Due / late is derived from payments made against the plan.
installments.x3: Reminders are queued by the night job.

expenses.s: Rent, bills, salaries, tea: write them in categories; close the day by counting the galla.
expenses.e: Electricity Rs. 6,200 and tea Rs. 800 today; at night you count Rs. 45,200 in the galla against Rs. 45,000 expected: +200 is saved.
expenses.x1: An expense is a ledger entry against the chosen account; a correction cancels and re-posts.
expenses.x2: Owner drawings are kept apart and are never an expense.
expenses.x3: Expenses feed profit after expenses in every report.

audit.s: Profit, cash, udhaar, stock, sales, purchases, staff, repairs and len-den for any period, with print and Excel.
audit.e: This month: net sales Rs. 7,18,800, gross profit, expenses, real profit; who sold what; which phones are 90 days old.
audit.x1: Read-only: every figure is derived from the ledger, documents and device events, and can be drilled down to the bill.
audit.x2: Periods, an "as of" day and the previous period; reconciliation checks that the books balance.
audit.x3: Cost and profit only for the owner and manager; the security feed only for the owner.

staff.s: Owner, manager, salesman, technician: each sees only what their work needs. Attendance and an activity log.
staff.e: Kashif (salesman) sells and adds stock but never sees the buying price or the shop's profit; Imran (manager) sees reports.
staff.x1: A role → capability matrix is checked on the server for every request, not only hidden in the screen.
staff.x2: Every action is in an audit log with who and when.
staff.x3: Price-rule overrides need the owner / manager PIN.

barcodes.s: Every phone and item gets a barcode; print price stickers and repair stickers; scan with any scanner.
barcodes.e: Scan a sticker at the counter: the phone is added to the sale. Scan the shelf: the stock count shows what is missing.
barcodes.x1: A barcode is given inside the purchase transaction and never changes; uniqueness spans phones, items, IMEIs and SKUs.
barcodes.x2: Code 128 / EAN / QR; any USB / Bluetooth scanner works as a keyboard.

help.t: Urdu, Roman Urdu, English — and a "?" everywhere
help.s: The app shows one language at a time; every field, card and tab has a "?" with an explanation and an example.
help.e: Not sure what "Net sales" means? Tap the "?": "Sales after discounts and returns — sold Rs. 1,20,000, one came back Rs. 40,000 → Rs. 80,000".
help.x1: All text comes from translation files; the bills and messages follow the shop's language.
help.x2: 1,100+ help terms, each with title, explanation and example in three languages.
help.x3: A test fails the build if any "?" misses a language or an example.

devices.s: Works on any phone browser, as an Android app, on a laptop with keyboard shortcuts, or on one Windows PC without internet.
devices.e: Internet goes: the sale waits on the phone and is sent once the connection is back. At home you check the audit on the laptop.
devices.x1: A PWA (installable web app) and a Capacitor Android app from the same code.
devices.x2: Offline sales are queued with an idempotency key so they are sent once.
devices.x3: The one-PC Windows install keeps its own database and checks in with the provider.

security.s: Your shop's data is only yours; every change is recorded; nothing is deleted.
security.e: A salesman cancels a bill: the owner sees it in the security feed with who, when and why.
security.x1: Every table is scoped by shop; no query can read another shop's rows.
security.x2: Money is exact (decimal, never floating point); the ledger and device events are append-only.
security.x3: Fingerprint / PIN login, phone OTP for a forgotten password, daily backups.

fbr.s: A full tax invoice on every bill, and — for registered shops — every bill sent to FBR with its number and QR.
fbr.e: Bilal sells a charger and a cover for Rs. 2,360 with 18% tax: the bill shows Rs. 2,000 excl. tax, "Tax 18% on 2,000 = 360", the amount in words, and the FBR number with its QR.
fbr.x1: The bill is queued in the same transaction as the sale and sent outside it, in the background and every minute by the scheduler.
fbr.x2: A claim stops two workers sending the same bill; an accepted bill is never posted again; retries back off from 1 to 60 minutes.
fbr.x3: The token is encrypted on the server and write-only: no screen or API ever returns it.

books.s: What the shop owns (stock, cash, udhaar to collect), owes (suppliers, len-den) and the owner's equity, on any date.
books.e: On 30 June: stock Rs. 18,40,000, cash and bank Rs. 2,15,000, customers owe Rs. 95,000, suppliers are owed Rs. 3,10,000 — the rest is your capital and profit.
books.x1: Built from the append-only ledger; nothing is typed in by hand.
books.x2: Trial balance: every account's debit and credit side by side, always equal.
books.x3: Corrections are new dated entries, so an old report never changes without a trace.

transfers.s: Send phones and accessories from one of your shops to another, and see what is on the way.
transfers.e: Gulberg branch sends 3 iPhones and 20 chargers to the Mall Road branch; the phones leave Gulberg's stock and arrive in Mall Road's with their full history.
transfers.x1: A phone row never changes shop: the sender records "transferred out", the receiver "transferred in".
transfers.x2: Items leave oldest batch first and arrive as a batch at that cost.
transfers.x3: Money moves at cost through a branch account, never as income; owner or manager only, same business.

android.p2: Barcode and CNIC scan with the camera

landing.metaTitle: Mobile Shop Software Pakistan — Android app, online & offline
landing.metaDesc: Mobile shop software for Pakistan: used and new phones with CNIC verification and the seller's signed consent, udhaar khata, repairs and repair labs, FBR-ready tax bills, branches, balance sheet, shop audit. Android app, online and offline, Urdu and English. 14 days free.

fbr.title: Bills ready for FBR
fbr.sub: For shops registered for sales tax. Built to FBR's Digital Invoicing rules (PRAL), so the day your shop has to report its invoices, you only switch it on.
fbr.p1: Every sale bill is sent to FBR right after the sale — no extra step at the counter.
fbr.p2: The FBR invoice number and its QR code print on the bill.
fbr.p3: Internet or FBR down? The bill waits and goes by itself; a sale is never stopped.
fbr.p4: Each bill goes once, never twice; a bill FBR turns down shows the reason and a "Send again" button.
fbr.p5: Your FBR token stays locked on the server and is never shown again, not even to you.
fbr.p6: Sale type and HS code per kind of goods — phones, other devices, accessories.
fbr.note: Off by default. You need your NTN, STRN and the IRIS Digital Invoicing token; we switch it on with you after a test with FBR's sandbox. Not registered for sales tax? Nothing changes for you.

audit.hint: Every rupee, phone and person for any period: sales, profit, money, debt, stock
audit.transfersNote: Moved between own accounts (not counted above):
audit.balances: Balances: start → end of the period
audit.limitations: Not recorded, so not shown: due dates on bills (debt age counts from the bill), tax on purchases, remittance fees.

fin.ofWhichTransfers: of which moved between own accounts
fin.noTax: No taxed bill in this period

rank.hint: Top customers and suppliers by the metric you pick; tap a person for their whole journey.

metric.suppliers_profit: Suppliers by profit on their phones

udhaar.ageHint: Bills carry no due date, so the age counts from the oldest unpaid bill; nothing is called overdue.
udhaar.notes: A bill with several phones shows the bill's remaining amount on each phone.
udhaar.overdueHint: Only bills with a promise date can be overdue; the rest show the age of the debt below.
udhaar.plansNote: Installment bills are already inside "people owe us" above; this shows which part is on installments.

inv.dimsHint: Each phone is counted once per dimension (a used PTA-approved phone is in both). Tap to open the list.
inv.ageHint: Age counts from the day the phone came in on its current round, not from its last note or price change. Bands are the shop's own thresholds.
inv.bypasses: Skipped ID checks (“I know this person”)
inv.bypassHint: Every skip is recorded with who did it and why; it never counts as a completed check. 'Unusual' follows the thresholds in Settings.
inv.noBypass: No skipped check in this period

prefs.bandsOrder: Each band must end after the one before it.

prod.soldVsBought: Sold (green) vs bought (amber) over the period
prod.thresholds: Top = {{top}}% of units or more · Low = {{low}} unit(s) or fewer

doc.noVoid: Nothing was voided in this period

sec.hint: Owner only. Every record here is immutable: a device event, an audit entry or a finalised bill — who did what, when, before → after, why, and who approved it.
sec.ownerOnly: The security audit is for the owner only.
sec.none: Nothing of this kind in the period
sec.notes: A finalised bill cannot be edited; a mistake is a void (listed here) and a new bill. Wrong owner PINs on price approvals are recorded; login failures are not recorded per user.

chart.moneyByKind: Money by account type (end of period)

rep.fullHint: Pick the sections, choose summary or detail, and get one report for the chosen period: a printable page (Save as PDF) or an Excel workbook with a sheet per section. The numbers are the same the screens show.
rep.footer: Every report states its period, the as-of day for balances, the currency (PKR) and what is not recorded.
rep.individualHint: Each one downloads as PDF, Excel or CSV; period reports follow the period chosen above.

sale.effect: The sale is cancelled and kept in the record as Deleted. The phone / items go back into stock, the money taken comes out of the galla and any udhaar comes off the customer's khata. Profit reports no longer count it.
sale.example: Samsung A15 sold for Rs. 38,000, Rs. 30,000 paid → the A15 is back in stock, Rs. 30,000 out of the galla, Rs. 8,000 off Bilal's khata.

purchase.effect: The purchase is cancelled and kept as Deleted. The phone / items leave stock, the money you paid comes back into the galla and the dealer's khata goes back to what it was. Not possible once the phone was sold or returned.
purchase.example: iPhone 12 bought for Rs. 90,000, Rs. 50,000 paid → the iPhone leaves stock, Rs. 50,000 back into the galla, Rs. 40,000 off Ali Traders' khata.

repair.effect: The repair job is cancelled and kept as Deleted. An advance taken is reversed, an open lab trip is cancelled and a shop phone goes back to stock.
repair.example: Screen job with Rs. 2,000 advance → Rs. 2,000 out of the galla (give it back), the job shows Deleted.

payment.effect: The payment is cancelled and kept as Deleted. The money goes back out of / into the galla, the person's khata is as it was before, and bills it paid show unpaid again.
payment.example: Received Rs. 10,000 from Bilal → galla −10,000, Bilal owes Rs. 10,000 again.

lending.effect: The len-den is cancelled and kept as Deleted. The money goes back to the galla or out of it, and the person's khata is as it was before.
lending.example: Gave Rs. 5,000 to Imran by mistake → Rs. 5,000 back in the galla, Imran owes nothing for it.

expense.effect: The expense is cancelled and kept crossed out. The money comes back into the galla / account and the profit report no longer counts it.
expense.example: Tea Rs. 500 typed as 5,000 → Rs. 5,000 back into the galla; then add Rs. 500 again, or use Edit instead.

exchange.effect: The whole exchange is cancelled: the new phone's sale and the old phone's purchase are both Deleted. The new phone comes back into stock, the old one goes back to the customer, a refund paid out is reversed and the khata is as before.
exchange.example: Old A12 taken at Rs. 20,000 for a new A15 at Rs. 38,000 → the A15 is back in stock, the A12 leaves stock, the galla and Bilal's khata are as before the exchange.

party.effect: If this person has no bills or payments, the name is removed. If they have, they are only hidden from lists — their old bills stay. Their khata must be zero first.
party.example: Customer added twice by mistake, no bills → removed. Old customer with bills → hidden, the bills stay.

accessory.effect: If this item was never bought or sold, it is removed. Otherwise it is hidden and its old bills stay. Its stock must be 0 first.
accessory.example: Cover typed with the wrong name, never sold → removed.

oldStock.effect: The phone added as old stock leaves stock and its cost comes out of the stock value. Only while it is still in stock and nothing was done with it.
oldStock.example: Oppo A57 added twice as opening stock at Rs. 25,000 → one removed, stock value −25,000.

cashAccount.effect: An account with no entries is removed. One that has entries is hidden; its history stays.
cashAccount.example: Bank account added by mistake, never used → removed.

expenseCategory.effect: A category with no expenses is removed. One that is in use cannot be deleted — rename it instead.
expenseCategory.example: 'Tea' added twice, the second never used → removed.

catalogue.effect: A brand, model, storage or colour you added is removed, only if no phone uses it.
catalogue.example: Model typed 'Galxy A15', never used → removed.

held.effect: The held cart is thrown away. Nothing was sold, so stock, galla and khata do not change.
held.example: Cart held for a customer who left → removed, the phone stays in stock.

labTrip.effect: The lab trip is cancelled: the phone counts as back at the shop. No money moves (the lab had not charged).
labTrip.example: Sent to Ali Lab by mistake → the trip is cancelled, the job is back with the shop.

saleReturn.effect: The return is undone and kept as Deleted. The phone / items go back to the customer as sold, the money handed back comes back into the galla, and the bill and khata are as before the return. Not possible once the phone was sold again or moved.
saleReturn.example: Bilal returned an A15 and got Rs. 30,000 back, by mistake → the A15 is his again, Rs. 30,000 back in the galla, the bill shows paid.

purchaseReturn.effect: The return to the dealer is undone and kept as Deleted. The phone / items come back into stock, the money the dealer gave back goes out of the galla, and the purchase and khata are as before. Not possible once the phone was bought again or moved.
purchaseReturn.example: iPhone returned to Ali Traders with Rs. 25,000 back, by mistake → the iPhone is in stock again, Rs. 25,000 out of the galla.

stockAdjust.effect: The adjustment is undone: the count goes back, and the stock loss (or extra stock) is taken out of the books. Both lines stay in the item's history.
stockAdjust.example: −3 covers marked lost, then found → +3 back, stock value as before, no stock loss.

cashTransfer.effect: The move is undone: the money goes back to the account it came from. Both lines stay, crossed out. It was never income or expense, so profit does not change.
cashTransfer.example: Rs. 50,000 moved from the galla to Meezan Bank by mistake → the galla +50,000, the bank −50,000.

loan.effect: The loan is cancelled: the phone is back in your stock and the loan shows Cancelled. No money moved on a loan, so nothing else changes.
loan.example: A15 lent to the wrong shop by mistake → the A15 is in stock again.

branchTransfer.effect: Everything comes back the way it went: the phones and items return from the other branch at the same cost, by a transfer back. Not possible once something there was sold or moved on.
branchTransfer.example: 2 phones and 4 cables sent to Branch 2 by mistake → back in this shop, Branch 2 has none of them.

installment.effect: The plan stops: no more due dates or reminders. What is left on the bill stays on the customer's khata as normal udhaar. Installments already collected stay. After this the sale itself can be deleted, if that was the mistake.
installment.example: Phone sold on 5 installments by mistake, Rs. 45,000 left → the plan stops, Ahmed owes Rs. 45,000 as udhaar.
